wet's flow in a seasonal window on FWA segments, on the segment MAD came from

Source: R/link_flow.R
knw_link_flow_window.Rd

knw_link_flow() reads the annual flow (MAD). This reads the mean flow over a window of the year, such as 1 August to 30 September, so a stream can be sized by what it carries when a life stage is in it (#226). The flow is wet's monthly flow (discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly, scenario historical) on the source wet picks for the segment, averaged over the window's days with each day taking its month's mean (wet::wet_flow_window(), the monthly basis).

Usage

knw_link_flow_window(conn, linear_feature_id, windows)

Arguments

conn

a DBI connection to a database holding discharge and whse_basemapping.

linear_feature_id

numeric FWA segment ids.

windows

data.frame with start and end, each "MM-DD", one row per window. A window whose end is before its start crosses 1 January.

Value

A tibble, one row per segment, ordered by linear_feature_id: linear_feature_id, mad_pick, and one column per window named by its dates, flow_<mmdd>_<mmdd> (m³/s).

Details

A window is read on the segment the annual flow came from: the segment's own, or the parent knw_link_flow() falls back to. So a window flow is present exactly where mad_pick is, on the same source, and mad_pick comes back beside it for a caller to hold to its own. A segment read must carry months 0 to 12 once each on one picked source, or the call stops: a window read from some of its months, or across two sources, is not that window's flow.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
knw_link_flow_window(conn, c(701747495, 701747496), data.frame(start = "08-01", end = "09-30"))
} # }
